memory_update.text: AAON should be tracked as an HVAC-labeled but increasingly data-center-cooling-exposed name; key evidence is BASX sales, backlog growth, liquid-cooling mix, and data-center customer durability.
POWL maps to the electrical distribution/switchgear chokepoint; the USD 400M-plus data-center order is strong evidence, but the thesis must be tested for lumpiness and repeatability.
IESC maps to the qualified installer/custom infrastructure solutions lane; it is a second-order AI beneficiary where the bottleneck may be field execution capacity rather than proprietary components.
nVent and Atkore are strong near-miss candidates for a follow-up pass focused specifically on racks, CDUs, manifolds, intelligent PDUs, cable pathway, and electrical balance-of-system components.

For this node, market mapping should separate four sub-bottlenecks: integrated power/thermal platforms, specialized cooling equipment, medium-voltage/switchgear systems, and qualified electrical/MEP installation capacity.
